framework_rationale: The submission imports only tensorcircuit alongside standard scientific/optimization libraries (functools, jax, numpy, optax). All core quantum circuit construction, custom Kraus channel application, and expectation-value evaluation are performed via tensorcircuit (tc.DMCircuit, tc.Gate, tc.gates, c.select_gate, c.rxx, c.apply_general_kraus, c.expectation) on its JAX backend with complex128 precision. No other quantum framework is imported or used, and there is no raw simulator bypass.
cheating_rationale: No signs of cheating, hardcoding, test/reward tampering, or evaluator exploitation. Synthetic target expectations are generated on the fly by running the noisy probe circuits at config['true_p01'] and config['true_p10'], and the trainable parameters are initialized solely from config['initial_p01'] and config['initial_p10'] and optimized via gradients through the noisy circuits without leaking the true probabilities.
fidelity_rationale: The implementation faithfully matches every requirement of the problem statement: it constructs the three single-qubit asymmetric bit-flip Kraus operators K0, K1, K2 from first principles; prepares all four 12-qubit probe states (GHZ, (|01>+|10>)/sqrt(2) pairs, |0>^12, and |+>^12); applies the even-bond then odd-bond brickwork RXX(entangler_angle) layers with per-qubit Kraus noise after each entangler; evaluates all 12 single-site Z_i expectations plus the 12-qubit parity Z_0...Z_11 for a (4, 13) table; parameterizes probabilities via sigmoid of unconstrained scalars initialized to initial_p01 and initial_p10; runs exactly max_steps Adam updates at learning_rate with MSE loss and no early stopping, recording pre-update losses in loss_history; and returns the required NumPy dictionary without printing.
implementation_error_rationale: No obvious implementation errors were found. Kraus matrix definitions match the specified transition directions (K1 maps |1> to |0> with sqrt(p10), K2 maps |0> to |1> with sqrt(p01)) and are trace-preserving; probe preparation gates produce the exact specified states (including H on even qubits, X on odd qubits, and CNOT(2k, 2k+1) yielding (|01>+|10>)/sqrt(2)); TensorCircuit's rxx(theta) convention matches exp(-i theta X_i X_j / 2) and is consistent with the reported initial loss; and all config values and return shapes/dtypes are handled properly.
